turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, doctor. Well, what brings me in is... I just feel like I've got this motor humming right under my skin whenever I'm supposed to sit still. 

Like, if I'm in a staff meeting at work, or sitting through church event briefings, I just can't stay put. I always end up shifting around in my chair, standing up, or just trying to find some excuse to get up and move around. It's really starting to become a problem for me.

symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient describes shifting around in their chair, which indicates squirming or fidgeting.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient mentions standing up and finding excuses to get up and move around during staff meetings and briefings where remaining seated is expected.
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient explicitly describes an internal feeling of restlessness, stating they 'can't stay put' when supposed to sit still.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient describes feeling like they have a 'motor humming right under my skin', which aligns with the symptom of acting as if 'driven by a motor'.

turns.doctor_question: Does this restlessness happen only in situations where you're supposed to sit still, or does it occur at other times as well?
turns.patient_response:
No, it's pretty much all the time. Like, on my shifts—I work as a janitor—I just go from mopping to checking the trash to straightening chairs without really stopping. I just keep moving. 

And even at home, when you'd think I'd want to rest my feet... I'll get back and just start puttering around in the garage, or I'll be re-sorting my tools instead of actually sitting down after work. It's just hard to turn it off.

symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient describes being constantly in motion without stopping, both at work and at home, and finding it hard to 'turn it off' and sit down.

turns.doctor_question: Did you have trouble sitting still or felt overly restless when you were a child?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I did. I remember getting in trouble back in grade school quite a bit for it, actually. I was always popping out of my seat, or... well, talking over the teacher. I'd usually just rush ahead and start on things before the directions were even finished. My mother, she used to say I acted like I was wound too tight, even as a kid. So it's definitely not a new thing.

turns.doctor_question: Did you often interrupt others or blurt out answers before they finished speaking when you were in school?
